title: Mabo v Queensland (No 2) decision
summary: On 3 June 1992 the High Court of Australia decided Mabo v Queensland (No 2), a case begun in 1982 by Meriam people of Mer (Murray Island) in the Torres Strait, led by Eddie Mabo. By a six-to-one majority it overturned the doctrine of terra nullius, recognised the Meriam people's native title and applied the principles across Australia, paving the way for the Native Title Act 1993.

uncertainty.note: Decision date. The case began on 20 May 1982 (Queensland State Archives), a ten-year proceeding.

reviewer_note: Pin is on Mer, the land at issue; the judgment itself was delivered by the High Court of Australia (location not pinned). Eddie Mabo is described by the Museum of Australian Democracy as having led the legal action for the Meriam people. The 1993 Act is named by the MoAD and ANU pages.

beats.caption: Eddie Mabo and four other Meriam plaintiffs begin legal proceedings against Queensland and the Commonwealth over their ancestral land.
The High Court rules that terra nullius should not have been applied; the Meriam people hold native title to their land.
The Native Title Act 1993 follows the decision, letting First Nations communities claim native title over traditional homelands.
